reason: PR-11.5 fixes MF-4 from the Claude Max red-team review. The prior guard watched five hardcoded Substrate paths, which left contract-surface-included schemas and registries outside the mutation tripwire. The replacement keeps the same runtime invariant, but derives watched files from registry/contract-surface-registry.json include/exclude patterns.
user_intent_alignment_summary: The user explicitly requested PR-11.5 pre-push governance hardening and named MF-4 as a real blocker. The requested minimal fix was to derive watched Substrate files from the active contract surface and fence eval candidate paths, without overbuilding OS-level ACLs.
diff_review_summary: The hardcoded watch list was replaced with contract-surface-registry loading, active-surface selection, include/exclude pattern expansion, and deterministic hashing of every included file. The module docstring now states that this Python guard is not a substitute for process/filesystem isolation.
why_merge_not_sufficient: Keeping the hardcoded five-file watch list would preserve the exact blocker. The old invariant was preserved, but the implementation had to be generalized to the contract surface.
replacement_justification: Any file included in the Substrate consumer contract surface can now trigger mutation detection during eval minting. This matches the pre-push red-team fix request without adding new product scope.
alternatives_considered: Add more hardcoded files. Rejected because it would still drift as the contract surface evolves.
Implement OS-level filesystem ACLs. Rejected as explicitly out of scope for PR-11.5.
